messages:
Maria Gonzalez: @channel urgent: Starlight Health is trying to finish BAA onboarding and they flagged two things: 1) need an addendum + confirmation we can support customer-managed keys in an HSM (FIPS 140-2) and 2) they saw intermittent 500s and higher latency overnight that may have included request/response metadata. They want clarity on retention of logs that could contain PHI. I filed initial ticket SUP-78921 with their contact. Can compliance + SRE triage?

Ops Bot: Thanks Maria — ticket SUP-78921 created and assigned to eng-sre. Incident stub: INC-202457. Paging @Security Oncall and @Alex Cheng. :rotating_light:

Alex Cheng: picking this up. Maria — can you paste the exact customer wording and the timestamps for the errors? also include a sample request-id if they provided one. We need first/last seen to correlate in logs.

Maria Gonzalez: their message: "We observed 500s between 2024-06-12T01:12:15Z and 2024-06-12T02:03:40Z across our prod tokens route. Affected request IDs: rA1b2c3, rA1b2c9. We also saw unusually long tail latency ~2.3s p50->p99. Please confirm log retention and whether PHI could be present in logs exported to SIEM." Contact is emily@starlight.health.

Jordan Lee: Alex — quick triage notes: those timestamps line up with a model rollout on dedicated-hosting in us-east-1? Checking deploy tags now. If it was a model variant mismatch we might see 500s due to KV cache mismatch; if auth tokens expired we would see 401s instead.

Samir Khan: @Jordan I pulled the request traces for rA1b2c3 and rA1b2c9 — both show upstream model agent timeouts at ~15s, then our proxy returned 500. Attached snippet: 
```
trace: request_id=rA1b2c3, route=/v1/generate, upstream=response_timeout, upstream_latency=15010ms, proxy_latency=15030ms
trace: request_id=rA1b2c9, route=/v1/generate, upstream=response_timeout, upstream_latency=14980ms, error=connection-reset
```
No auth failures in those traces.

Alex Cheng: Good capture. That points to transient model worker slowness/timeouts. Did the customer run any high-batch jobs at that time? Maria, ask them for any large replay jobs or embedding jobs that could have spiky token churn.

Maria Gonzalez: They said a scheduled ingest job ran 01:00-01:30 UTC that sent long prompts (~6k tokens) to the generation endpoint. They thought those were rate-limited but not 500ing before.

Jordan Lee: long sequences + default timeout = plausible cause. For remediation: 1) recommend the customer reduce max_sequence for generation or use streaming with chunked prompts, 2) for infra we should consider increasing upstream timeouts or autoscale burst capacity for that Dedicated pool for now.

Security Oncall: on the compliance side: we must treat this as sensitive. Maria — do NOT ask them to paste any PHI into Slack. Request redacted logs or request IDs only. For audit logs and retention: our default hosted audit logs surface request metadata (request-id, route, timestamps, user id, account id) and are retained 30 days. For Dedicated/Private enterprise we have options: extended retention (365 days) and S3 export with encryption, and Private supports customer-managed KMS + HSM-backed keys.

Compliance Bot: Reference: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/compliance/hipaa (internal) — BAA and key options: 
- Hosted: BAA possible but requires elevated review; encryption at rest with provider-managed keys by default, CMEK via AWS KMS available for certain enterprise plans (not HSM).
- Dedicated & Private: support for CMEK + HSM-backed key wraps (FIPS 140-2) in Private deployments; on-prem HSM integrations available with Private package.

Alex Cheng: So for this customer (starlight) if they require HSM-wrapped keys for model and audit data we need to move them to Private or a Dedicated with a KMS bridge? We should surface tradeoffs: Private gives full control and audit logs never leave VPC; Hosted with CMEK still stores logs in our control plane if on Hosted.

Samir Khan: For the immediate outage/500s, steps I will run: correlate rA* traces to worker node IDs, check model-agent logs around 01:00-02:00 UTC, and capture worker memory/CPU spikes. Also collect autoscaler activity for that Dedicated pool. I'll paste redacted logs here once available.

Maria Gonzalez: Customer asked: "If audit logs contain prompt text, can you confirm purge/retention policies and how to get them redacted ASAP?"

Security Oncall: by default we do NOT store full prompt text in long-term audit logs exported to SIEM — request-level traces include metadata and sampling of payloads for debug only and are on a short retention. But we must verify for their account: sometimes debug-level sampling was enabled during onboarding. ACTION: Compliance to check whether sampling/debug hooks were enabled for starlight.health account at that time.

Jordan Lee: Quick repro for SRE: simulate a long prompt (6k tokens) via curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"<6k-token payload>","max_tokens":512}'
```
If we see upstream timeouts, adjust model-agent timeout config in infra: upstream.timeout_ms -> 30000.

Samir Khan: Update: found worker crash logs for node i-0abcde around 01:18 UTC — OOM kill after processing large KV cache warm-up. Crash explains the timeouts. Attaching redacted snippet: 
```
[01:18:23] oom_kill: process=model-agent pid=4521 rss=28GB vms=56GB
[01:18:23] reason=kernel-out-of-memory
```
We'll escalate to infra to increase memory or pin quantized model variant for that pool.

Compliance Bot: For BAA: to proceed we need a signed DPA/BAA template plus confirmation of customer key requirements. I can ping legal to stand up the addendum. For keys/HSM: ask customer to confirm whether they require HSM key material stored in their on-prem HSM or just HSM-backed KMS managed by cloud provider. We support both patterns but Private is recommended for strict control.

Maria Gonzalez: Emily (customer) replied: they require HSM with FIPS 140-2 and want audit exports with full request metadata but NO payload text stored. They also want confirmation that billing/invoice metadata will not contain PHI.

Security Oncall: billing metadata (account id, invoice amounts) never contains user prompt text. We'll provide a formal statement. ACTIONS: 1) Compliance to draft BAA addendum + KMS/HSM spec 2) SRE/Infra to propose immediate mitigations for the OOM/crash 3) Product to confirm export retention options and guarantee removal of payload text in exports.

Alex Cheng: I'll open infra ticket INFRA-6128 to adjust worker sizing for that Dedicated pool and add a canary config to pin to quantized variant for high-length requests. Also recommend a short-term config change: enable request-level payload sampling off for starlight account to zero to avoid storing prompt text. Need Product + Compliance sign-off.

Samir Khan: Will redact and paste compressed crash log: 
```
[redacted] oom_kill at 01:18:23 node i-0abcde
[redacted] recent-restart-count=1
[redacted] affected-requests=[rA1b2c3,rA1b2c9]
```
No prompt text included.

Compliance Bot: I've started a doc draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/secure/BAA-starlight-draft (internal). Will add the KMS options matrix and the retention SLA (30/90/365 days) and export formats.

Maria Gonzalez: customer wants timeline: when can we 1) confirm HSM support and addendum, 2) provide log redaction confirmation, and 3) resolve backend 500s.

Security Oncall: timeline estimate: 1) BAA + HSM: draft within 2 business days, legal review 5-7 business days (may be quicker) 2) log redaction confirmation: immediate check — if sampling was on we can flip off and confirm within 24 hours and provide export showing no payloads 3) backend 500s: infra mitigation (increase worker memory / pin quantized model) within 4-8 hours, full long-term capacity plan in 3-5 days.

Alex Cheng: tagging INFRA-6128, SUP-78921, INC-202457. I'll coordinate the infra change now. Please keep all PHI out of Slack. Use redacted IDs for follow-ups.

Maria Gonzalez: I'll relay timeline to Emily and share next updates here. Thanks everyone. :pray:
